62158-a-letter-addressed-to-the-right-ho:
Evan Evans wrote a long letter in eighteen thirty-two to Lord Robert Grosvenor, a member for Chester. Evans served as chaplain to the Chester Cambrian Society. The society had been set up about six years before to give Welsh folk in Chester church teaching in their own tongue. It worked with the Church of England, and its gains had passed all hopes.

Some still doubt that Welsh services are right or wise, and say Welsh folk should learn English. Evans sets out to test that claim. He first tells how the group began as a Welsh social club, the Cymmrodorion Society. Its members then saw how poor Welsh workers in Chester lacked teaching they could grasp, and changed their aim.
